If you just picked up a new Mac, like the recently released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you may also be on the hunt for a new external display.

Below are my recommendations, covering a range of product categories, price points, and other factors.

Best Mac external monitors

Apple Studio Display

Any best monitor recommendation would be remiss not to include Apple's Studio Display. While it commands a premium price tag, it features Apple's signature elegant design and comes equipped with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color support: Wide color gamut (P3), supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • True Tone technology: Automatically adjusts display color temperature based on ambient light
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display comes in multiple configurations at different price points, which I'll list one by one. If you want an iMac-like experience with your Mac, the Apple Studio Display is the obvious choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR launched earlier this year, bringing several major upgrades over the regular Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR, up to 2,000 nits HDR peak
  • Color support: Wide P3 and Adobe RGB color gamuts, supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 120Hz, with Adaptive Sync support
  • Host charging: Up to 140W

Of course, these advantages also come with a higher price tag than the regular Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor features a 4K OLED panel, making it extremely appealing for Mac users. My colleague Justin Kahn at 9to5Toys has switched to this display and says, "I've really enjoyed using it with my Mac mini over the past few months."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2 USB-A
  • Built-in camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

While it doesn't offer the crisp 5K or 6K resolution of some other choices, you'll get to enjoy the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks and superior color reproduction and contrast.

Buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K represents LG's evolution in the high-end monitor market. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels and offers a generous selection of ports. Here are the key specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • True Tone technology: None; supports automatic brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast ratio: 2,000:1

LG UltraFine 6K purchase link

Asus ProArt 5K monitor

My colleague Jeff Benjamin had hands-on experience with this product, which immediately caught my attention. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K monitor offers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880) and similar 27-inch size as the Studio Display, but at half the price.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz, with Adaptive-Sync support
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Ambient light and backlight sensors automatically adjust brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

For all the details, check out Jeff's full review. If you're in the market for a 5K monitor for your Mac, the Asus ProArt is hard to beat.

Asus ProArt Display 5K purchase link:

Asus ProArt 6K monitor

If you're looking for something bigger with higher resolution, Asus has you covered as well. The new Asus ProArt Display 6K (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch monitor with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "outrageously good value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz, with Adaptive-Sync support (48–60Hz)
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub connections, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

Perhaps the biggest selling point of the ASUS ProArt 6K monitor is its price. It's significantly cheaper than some of the most popular 4K and 5K monitors on the market.

ASUS ProArt 6K monitor purchase link:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

The Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K is another attractive option to pair with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: 350 nits typical
  • Color support: 99% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness based on ambient light
  • Ports: One USB-C port with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A ports, one downstream USB-C port, Ethernet, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K purchase link:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt monitor

This might just be my favorite pick on this list right now. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor comes with a host of Mac-friendly features, and its headline feature is of course its sharp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical and peak; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C port, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: A physical external controller with customizable buttons

BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor purchase link:

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt monitor

If you're looking to pair a 32-inch monitor with your new Mac for under $1,000, this is one of the most attractive options out there. The biggest drawback, however, is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. That said, it offers a generous selection of ports and delivers a 32-inch panel at a price below $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Color support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustment: No automatic ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, USB-B, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt monitor purchase link:

Dell U4025QW 40-inch ultrawide monitor

If you're looking to pair an ultrawide monitor with your Mac, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options on the market. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch display, along with a wealth of ports, a matte screen, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: Up to 120Hz, with VRR support
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Ambient light sensor automatically adjusts brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C ports, five USB-A ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Dell U4025QW 40-inch ultrawide monitor purchase link:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

For a more budget-friendly entry into the ultrawide monitor market, consider the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC, which is currently selling at nearly half price. While it lacks some of the bells and whistles of other options, you still get a 34-inch ultrawide curved display and a generous selection of ports, including a Thunderbolt 4 port that supports power delivery.

  • Display: 34-inch ultrawide curved display, Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1000R curvature, offering an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: 350 nits typical.
  • Camera: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (providing up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0 port, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0 ports, one RJ45 Ethernet port, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC purchase link:

Summary

These are just some of the best external monitor options to pair with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, a wealth of connectivity options, and unique sizes and designs.

Did you recently buy a new Mac? Which monitor are you using with it? Let us know in the comments.
